question: Should Microsoft Teams officially support multiple bot accounts through `channels.msteams.accounts` and `defaultAccount` while retaining the root-level single-bot shape?
rationale: The implementation is technically sound, but it creates a permanent public configuration, authentication, routing, setup, and persisted-state contract that automation cannot accept on the project’s behalf.

options.title: Close pending sponsorship
options.body: Do not accept the new Teams contract until a responsible owner explicitly sponsors and maintains the direction.

options.title: Sponsor the full contract
options.body: Reopen and land the branch after owner review confirms the complete config, upgrade, credential, and state-isolation contract.

options.title: Sponsor a narrower first release
options.body: Reopen with core bot identity and routing support while deferring selected Graph, delegated-auth, setup, or state surfaces.

recommendation.title: Close pending sponsorship
recommendation.body: Do not accept the new Teams contract until a responsible owner explicitly sponsors and maintains the direction.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is the strongest available routing signal for the Teams product decision and is already connected to adjacent Teams work.
